symbols.description: A narrow band of strong wind and a type of air current that forms high in the atmosphere.
symbols.name: jet stream

symbols.description: Moving air; the source describes a jet stream as a type of wind and air current.
symbols.name: wind

symbols.description: The planet whose atmosphere, surface, poles, equator, and jet streams are discussed.
symbols.name: Earth

symbols.description: The source of heat that does not heat the whole Earth evenly.
symbols.name: Sun

symbols.description: The gaseous region around Earth in which air masses and jet streams occur.
symbols.name: atmosphere

symbols.description: The layer of Earth's atmosphere where people live and breathe, including its mid to upper region.
symbols.name: troposphere

symbols.description: The surface of Earth used as the reference for jet-stream altitude.
symbols.name: Earth's surface

symbols.description: One of the two primary jet streams near the north and south poles.
symbols.name: polar jet stream

symbols.description: One of the two primary jet streams located closer to the equator.
symbols.name: subtropical jet stream

symbols.description: The northern polar region near one of the polar jet streams.
symbols.name: north pole

symbols.description: The southern polar region near one of the polar jet streams.
symbols.name: south pole

symbols.description: The region referenced as having warmer areas and as being nearer to the subtropical jet streams.
symbols.name: equator

symbols.description: An air mass with higher temperature that rises when it meets a cooler air mass.
symbols.name: warm air mass

symbols.description: An air mass with lower temperature that sinks when it meets a warmer air mass.
symbols.name: cold air mass

symbols.description: Cold air from the Arctic referenced in relation to the jet stream and storm conditions.
symbols.name: Arctic air

symbols.description: The event in which warm and cold air masses meet in the atmosphere.
symbols.name: air-mass meeting

symbols.description: The Sun's uneven heating of Earth, associated with warmer equatorial areas and colder polar areas.
symbols.name: uneven solar heating

symbols.description: The upward movement of warmer air higher in the atmosphere.
symbols.name: air rising

symbols.description: The downward movement of cooler air to replace warmer air.
symbols.name: air sinking

symbols.description: The creation of an air current by the movement of warm and cool air masses.
symbols.name: air-current formation

symbols.description: The formation of a jet stream when warm and cold air masses meet in the atmosphere.
symbols.name: jet-stream formation

symbols.description: The difference between the temperatures of warm and cool air masses.
symbols.name: temperature difference

symbols.description: The speed at which a jet stream moves, including average and higher speeds.
symbols.name: jet-stream speed

symbols.description: The height of a jet stream above Earth's surface.
symbols.name: jet-stream altitude

symbols.description: The general direction in which Earth's primary jet streams travel.
symbols.name: west-to-east direction

symbols.description: Bulges of winds created when jet streams move in different ways toward the north and south.
symbols.name: northward and southward wind bulges

symbols.description: The season in which very high speeds usually occur in polar jet streams.
symbols.name: winter

symbols.description: An aircraft that can fly in the mid to upper troposphere and receive a boost from a jet stream.
symbols.name: airplane

symbols.description: An increase in an airplane's travel advantage when it flies in the same direction as a powerful jet stream.
symbols.name: airplane boost

symbols.description: A route traveled by an airplane, including west-to-east and east-to-west travel along the same route.
symbols.name: air-travel route

symbols.description: A system that fast-moving air currents can transport and that may remain in place when far from a jet stream.
symbols.name: weather system

symbols.description: The geographic region across which jet streams can transport weather systems.
symbols.name: United States

symbols.description: A property of air and weather referenced in relation to heating, air masses, and weather effects.
symbols.name: temperature

symbols.description: A weather outcome affected by weather systems transported by jet streams.
symbols.name: precipitation

symbols.description: A period of heat that can result when a weather system remains in one place.
symbols.name: heat wave

symbols.description: A condition that can result when a weather system remains in one place.
symbols.name: flood

symbols.description: A weather event that tends to follow the edge of a jet stream.
symbols.name: storm

symbols.description: The boundary of a jet stream that storms tend to follow.
symbols.name: jet-stream edge

symbols.description: Conditions created by the difference between cool and warm air where storms form or follow the jet-stream edge.
symbols.name: turbulent conditions

symbols.description: An atmospheric phenomenon associated with warmer and wetter air meeting colder Arctic air near a displaced jet stream.
symbols.name: thunder

symbols.description: An atmospheric phenomenon associated with warmer and wetter air meeting colder Arctic air near a displaced jet stream.
symbols.name: lightning

symbols.description: A severe weather event associated with the conditions near a southward-displaced jet stream.
symbols.name: tornado
